title: Initial perf-canary runner: config, model matrix, prompt set loader, streaming/non-streaming
author: Marcus Reed
body:
Implements the initial perf-canary runner service and supporting libraries. This is the first end-to-end slice needed to generate repeatable inference traffic across a small model set without impacting customer queues (full isolation/routing comes in follow-ups).

What’s included in this PR: runner service skeleton with a single binary (cmd/perf-canary) that reads a config file, loads a model list + prompt sets, and executes a scheduled workload loop; supports both streaming and non-streaming request modes (with a common request envelope) so we can compare latency + tokens/sec computations later; prompt set loader (jsonl) with deterministic sampling and optional per-shape weighting (so we can keep stability while still exercising multiple prompt/response lengths); a minimal workload matrix abstraction (model x region x mode x prompt_shape) with per-cell concurrency and rate limiting knobs; structured logging with stable fields required for triage (run_id, model, region, prompt_shape, mode, max_output_tokens, seed, and request_id); basic health endpoints (/livez, /readyz) and a lightweight metrics endpoint for runner-internal counters (not the runtime metrics spec yet).

Not included (intentional in v0): baseline computation/regression detection, alerting, deploy-window suppression, or runtime-specific tagging. Those will be added in subsequent PRs once the traffic generator is stable.

Config overview: The runner reads a single YAML config and supports env var overrides for secrets. Example snippet used in local + staging:

models:
  - name: "llama-3-70b-instruct"
    endpoint: "https://api.staging.redwoodinference.com/v1/chat/completions"
  - name: "qwen2.5-32b-instruct"
    endpoint: "https://api.staging.redwoodinference.com/v1/chat/completions"
regions: ["us-east", "eu-west"]
workloads:
  - model: "llama-3-70b-instruct"
    region: "us-east"
    mode: "streaming"
    prompt_set: "prompts/chat_short.jsonl"
    max_output_tokens: 256
    qps: 0.2
    concurrency: 2
  - model: "llama-3-70b-instruct"
    region: "us-east"
    mode: "non_streaming"
    prompt_set: "prompts/chat_long.jsonl"
    max_output_tokens: 512
    qps: 0.1
    concurrency: 1

Operational notes: The scheduler is intentionally simple (tick loop + per-workload token bucket) and prioritizes stability/traceability over maximum throughput. Each workload cell uses a bounded worker pool; in-flight requests are tracked so shutdown can be graceful. The runner records first-byte/first-token timestamps for streaming, and includes explicit timing fields for later tokens/sec calculation changes (see follow-up work).

Testing: Adds unit tests for prompt loading, deterministic sampling, and streaming event parsing. Includes a small golden prompt fixture. Also adds a minimal integration test that hits a mock SSE server to validate streaming parsing and timeout handling.

Rollout: this is safe to deploy in staging only. Prod deployment will wait for canary-safe routing + strict rate limits (ENG-2843 follow-up tasks).

Notes for reviewers: most of the code is new. The key pieces to sanity check are (1) config schema defaults and validation, (2) streaming parser correctness under partial frames, and (3) rate limiting behavior under concurrency.

Follow-ups: baseline/detector (PR #109), GPU/region tagging + routing (PR #113), alert payload enrichment (PR #118), variance reduction (warmup/cache priming) (PR #121).
commits: bootstrap runner skeleton (cobra CLI, config loading, structured logging)
add prompt set loader (jsonl) + deterministic sampling + fixtures
implement workload scheduler (tick loop, token bucket QPS limiter, bounded worker pools)
add streaming/non-streaming request clients + SSE parser + timeouts
add /livez /readyz + runner metrics endpoint + graceful shutdown
tests: prompt loader unit tests + streaming parser integration test (mock SSE server)
docs: local dev quickstart + sample configs
review_conversation:
Noah Patel: Overall direction looks good. Two asks: (1) ensure we record both "first token" and "last token" timestamps for streaming so tokens/sec isn’t ambiguous later; (2) add a hard cap on max in-flight per workload to avoid surprises if QPS limiter misbehaves.

Marcus Reed (author): Added FirstTokenAt/LastTokenAt fields to the streaming response stats and wired them through the logger. Also added MaxInFlight (default = concurrency * 2) with a clear log line when we skip scheduling due to saturation.

Sofia Ivanova: Scheduler loop: can we make the tick interval configurable and jittered? We’ve seen synchronized tickers create burstiness across replicas.

Marcus Reed: Added tick_interval_ms to config and a small random jitter (+/- 10%) per workload cell on each tick. Also added a note in README about keeping intervals >= 500ms for low-footprint behavior.

Nadia Rahman: Prompt sampling: please make sure the seed is visible and stable in logs for replay. Also, loader should validate required columns/fields to avoid silent empty prompts.

Marcus Reed: Seed is now part of run_id and emitted as seed=<int>. Loader validates required fields ("id", "messages" or "prompt") depending on mode; on validation failure runner refuses to start.

Rafael Mendes: For oncall: add /readyz to return non-200 if config fails validation or if all workloads are disabled. Also please include a single-line "startup summary" log listing active workloads.

Marcus Reed: /readyz now checks (a) config validation ok, (b) at least one workload enabled, (c) credentials loaded. Added a startup summary log line with a compact table (model/region/mode/prompt_set/qps/concurrency).

Noah Patel: LGTM after last push. This is a solid v0. Please keep the public surface small; we’ll iterate quickly.

Sofia Ivanova: Approved.

Nadia Rahman: Approved.

Rafael Mendes: Approved, thanks for making /readyz semantics explicit.
release_notes: Internal: adds initial perf-canary runner capable of issuing streaming and non-streaming inference traffic from a declarative workload config (staging only).
